headline: KSE-100 slips 348 points as KP emergency vote slides to Thursday, while Tadawul rebounds and Fed December-hike odds ease to 72%
mood: Cautiously mixed · politics still the swing factor for Pakistan

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Gives Back 348 Points as KP Vote Slips to Thursday
five_things.html: The KSE-100 opened over 900 points higher on hopes of a quick resolution to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa crisis, but late selling flipped the session, leaving the index down 347.97 points (−0.21%) to close at 164,776.44 after swinging between an intraday high of 166,070.48 and a low of 164,773.67. Buying held in autos, cement, banks, oil & gas exploration and OMCs (LUCK, DGKC, HBL, MCB, MEBL, NBP, OGDC, MARI, PSO all traded green intraday) before profit-taking took hold; market-wide shares traded rose to 383.75 million from 362.95 million the prior session. The catalyst: the National Assembly and Senate sessions called for 6pm Tuesday did not ratify the KP Governor's Rule as expected — a joint sitting has now been pushed to Thursday, 15 October at 11am, extending the political overhang by two more trading days. Business Recorder and Capital News Point confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Tadawul Rebounds Above 10,300 After Riyadh Airport Attack
five_things.html: Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All-Share Index rose 34.18 points (+0.33%) to close at 10,318.14 on Tuesday, recovering from Monday's attack-driven dip, on turnover of SR3.28bn (~$875m) though breadth stayed soft at 104 advancers to 146 decliners; the parallel Nomu index added 0.37% to 22,030.36 and the MSCI Tadawul 30 gained 0.37% to 1,388.2. The bounce came even as the Strait of Hormuz/tanker-attack risk overhang persisted, with Saudi forces reported striking Houthi positions. Arab News and Kitco confirm the moves.

five_things.chip: Fed December Hike Odds Ease to ~72% as Yields Stay Elevated
five_things.html: Fed-funds futures now price roughly 72% odds of a December rate hike, down from last week's ~88% pricing, even as the 10-year Treasury held near 5.21% and the 2-year near 4.81% with the 30-year dipping below 5.58%. A softer-but-still-elevated dollar and the persistent Hormuz supply-risk overhang pulled gold down 0.24% to $4,160.80 and silver down 1.82% to $59.09 as traders de-risked ahead of Wednesday's US CPI print. Kitco and Trading Economics confirm the pricing.
five_things.sentiment: odds cool slightly, yields still restrictive

five_things.chip: Pakistan's September CPI Confirmed at 10.3% as SBP Holds at 11.5%
five_things.html: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics data confirm September CPI eased to 10.3% y/y from 11.1% in August, still well above the SBP's 5–7% target band; the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% at its 14 September meeting for a third straight hold, with the next decision due 26 October. Three-month KIBOR sat at 11.76–12.01% as of 12 October, and USD/PKR held virtually flat at 276.96 interbank (+Re0.01). The IMF's $1.2bn fourth EFF/third RSF tranche remains pending Executive Board sign-off. The Nation and Trading Economics confirm the figures.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Slips as Chip Weakness Offsets Bank Earnings
five_things.html: US stocks closed lower Tuesday as memory-chip weakness and crosscurrents from bank earnings outweighed otherwise solid results: the Dow fell 0.35% (−180.45 pts) to 51,670.10, the S&P 500 slipped 0.02% to 7,805.45 and the Nasdaq lost 0.15% to 27,204.38, with traders cautious ahead of Wednesday's inflation print. Separately, OPEC+ held November output quotas unchanged, while Brent settled near $105.67 (+0.8%) and WTI near $94.14 (+0.66%) as the Hormuz/Houthi risk premium persisted. TheStreet and Trading Economics confirm the details.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape stayed politically hostage: the KSE-100 opened over 900 points higher before late selling cut it to a close of 164,776.44, down 347.97 points (−0.21%), after the National Assembly and Senate sessions summoned for 6pm Tuesday failed to ratify the KP Governor's Rule as hoped — PPP has signalled it will back the government's resolution, but a joint sitting is now pushed to Thursday, 15 October. Index-heavy names (LUCK, DGKC, HBL, MCB, MEBL, OGDC, PSO) traded green intraday on hopes of a quick resolution, and market-wide volume rose to 383.75m shares from 362.95m, before profit-taking reasserted itself. The macro backdrop stayed constructive: September CPI confirmed at 10.3% y/y, the SBP held at 11.5% for a third straight meeting, the rupee held flat at 276.96 interbank, and the $1.2bn IMF tranche still awaits Executive Board approval. Business Recorder and The Nation.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf markets stabilised after Monday's security shock: Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All-Share Index rebounded 0.33% to close at 10,318.14 on SR3.28bn turnover, though breadth stayed soft (104 advancers vs 146 decliners), while the Nomu parallel market added 0.37% and the MSCI Tadawul 30 gained a similar margin — a sign risk appetite is returning even as the Hormuz/tanker-attack overhang persists with Saudi forces reportedly striking Houthi positions. Brent held near $105.67 and WTI near $94.14 after OPEC+ kept November quotas unchanged, giving Gulf energy names a steady tailwind. Diversification momentum stayed intact: Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI climbed to 55.3 in September, its strongest reading since February and a sixth straight month of growth, while the UAE's non-oil PMI held at 55.3 with output prices rising at their fastest pace in over 15 years. Arab News and The National.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street closed lower Tuesday as memory-chip weakness and mixed bank earnings outweighed an otherwise resilient tape: the Dow fell 0.35% to 51,670.10, the S&P 500 eased 0.02% to 7,805.45 and the Nasdaq lost 0.15% to 27,204.38, with traders positioning cautiously ahead of Wednesday's US CPI print. Treasury yields stayed elevated (10-year 5.21%, 2-year 4.81%, 30-year just below 5.58%) even as Fed-funds futures trimmed December hike odds to roughly 72% from last week's ~88%; the same mix of a softer-but-still-firm dollar and persistent geopolitical risk pulled gold down 0.24% to $4,160.80 and silver down 1.82% to $59.09. Washington's broader funding picture stays parked under the continuing resolution through 11 December, though the narrower DHS funding lapse remains unresolved separately. TheStreet and Kitco.

legislative.policy_html: KP Governor's Rule ratification slipped from Tuesday's NA/Senate sessions to a joint sitting now scheduled for Thursday, 15 October; PPP has signalled support while JUI-F has filed a Senate resolution opposing the move.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: the federal government and security apparatus retain administrative control pending the delayed vote, and defense-linked sentiment holds firm. Loses: banks and broader equities, which absorbed Tuesday's late-session reversal (KSE-100 down 348 points) as the extended political uncertainty pushes the risk premium two more trading days out.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+'s decision to hold November output quotas steady continues to anchor Gulf energy supply, alongside the UAE's VAT Executive Regulation amendments (Cabinet Decision No. 149) now in force since 1 October.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf oil producers and energy equities, which benefit from supply discipline plus the Hormuz/tanker-attack risk premium keeping Brent above $105; large UAE corporates and banks already compliant with the new VAT apportionment rules. Loses: UAE SMEs facing heavier VAT-compliance costs, and broader Gulf risk sentiment, which stayed cautious (Tadawul breadth 104 advancers vs 146 decliners) even as the index itself rebounded.

legislative.policy_html: Fed-funds futures trimmed December hike odds to ~72% from ~88% a week earlier, while the US continuing resolution funds the government through 11 December alongside an unresolved, narrower DHS funding lapse.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: near-term funding certainty for the broader government and bond markets as hike odds ease modestly, and energy equities riding the Hormuz risk premium. Loses: precious metals (gold −0.24%, silver −1.82% Tuesday) as yields stay elevated, and DHS-linked contractors/agencies still exposed to the unresolved funding lapse.

levels.support_note: first floor; deeper support at 162,500 if Thursday's vote disappoints
levels.resistance_note: Tuesday's intraday high; then 167,089 (Friday's close) if the KP vote clears cleanly

desk_stance_html: Tuesday's reversal — a 900-point intraday swing that still closed 348 points lower — shows the market wants to rally on KP resolution hopes but keeps getting stopped out when the vote slips, as it did again when Thursday's joint sitting replaced Tuesday's expected ratification. The macro base case still argues for a floor: September CPI at 10.3%, a steady SBP rate at 11.5%, a resilient rupee at 276.96, and a pending $1.2bn IMF tranche all work in the index's favour once the political overhang clears. Globally, Tadawul's rebound above 10,300 and softer (but still elevated) Fed hike odds are modest tailwinds, while persistent Hormuz-driven oil strength is a mixed signal for Pakistan's import bill. Our stance: stay selective into Thursday's vote, favour index-heavy banks and energy names only on confirmed breadth, and treat any push through 166,070 as a signal to watch for follow-through toward 167,089 rather than a reason to chase. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 slips 348 points as the KP ratification vote slides to Thursday, while Tadawul rebounds above 10,300 and Fed December-hike odds ease to roughly 72%.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US stocks closed lower Tuesday as memory-chip weakness and mixed bank earnings outweighed an otherwise resilient tape: the Dow fell 0.35% to 51,670.10, the S&P 500 eased 0.02% to 7,805.45 and the Nasdaq lost 0.15% to 27,204.38, with traders cautious ahead of Wednesday's US CPI print. Treasury yields stayed elevated (10Y 5.21%, 2Y 4.81%) even as Fed-funds futures trimmed December hike odds to roughly 72% from ~88% a week earlier; the same mix of a softer dollar and persistent geopolitical risk pulled gold down 0.24% to $4,160.80 and silver down 1.82% to $59.09.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 opened over 900 points higher on hopes of a quick KP resolution, but late selling flipped the session to a close of 164,776.44, down 347.97 points (-0.21%), after Tuesday's NA/Senate sessions failed to ratify the KP Governor's Rule as expected — a joint sitting is now set for Thursday, 15 October. Index-heavy banks, cement and energy names traded green intraday before profit-taking reasserted itself; market-wide volume rose to 383.75m shares from 362.95m. September CPI was confirmed at 10.3% y/y, the SBP held its rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting, and the rupee held flat at 276.96 interbank; the $1.2bn IMF tranche still awaits Executive Board approval.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All-Share Index rebounded 0.33% to close at 10,318.14 on SR3.28bn turnover, recovering from Monday's attack-driven dip even as breadth stayed soft (104 advancers vs 146 decliners) and the Hormuz/tanker-attack risk overhang persisted. Brent held near $105.67 and WTI near $94.14 after OPEC+ kept November quotas unchanged. Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI climbed to 55.3 in September, a six-month high, while the UAE's non-oil PMI held at the same level.

GLOBAL
Washington's funding picture stays parked under the continuing resolution through 11 December, though the narrower DHS funding lapse remains unresolved. Easing (but still elevated) Fed hike odds offered modest relief to rate-sensitive assets, while precious metals stayed under pressure from firm yields.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
- Pakistan: KP Governor's Rule ratification pushed to Thursday's joint sitting — the federal government/security apparatus retains control; banks and equities absorb two more days of political-risk premium.
- GCC: OPEC+ holding November output steady + UAE VAT rules now in force — oil producers and compliant corporates win; UAE SMEs and broader Gulf sentiment lag.
- Global: US funding certainty through 11 December vs. cooling-but-still-elevated Fed hike odds — bonds and the broader government stabilise; precious metals and DHS-linked contractors stay exposed.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 164,000 (deeper support 162,500 if Thursday's vote disappoints), pivot 164,776 (Tuesday's close), resistance 166,070 then 167,089 if the KP vote clears cleanly. Our stance: stay selective into Thursday's vote, favour index-heavy banks and energy names only on confirmed breadth, and treat a push through 166,070 as a signal to watch rather than a reason to chase. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
